kind.content: Craft · Essay 48
Why I write by hand first
Paper is slow, and slow is the point. On first drafts that are allowed to be bad.
MO
Mira Okafor · 14 September 2026 · 7 min read

kind.alt: Marbled endpaper in navy, oxblood and gold

kind.content: Every essay I have published here started the same way: on paper, in a notebook with a cracked spine, in handwriting only I can read. People ask whether that is nostalgia. It is not. It is the cheapest way I know to be allowed to be wrong.

A blank document is a stage. The cursor blinks like an impatient stage manager and every sentence arrives already typeset, already looking finished. Paper does not do that. On paper a sentence looks exactly as unfinished as it is.
Bad on purpose

The first draft has one job: to find out what I think. It is allowed to repeat itself, to start three times, to wander into a paragraph about my grandmother's handwriting and never come back. By hand, that is fine. Nobody will ever see it, including, most days, me.
On paper a sentence looks exactly as unfinished as it is.

Typing it up is the second draft, and it is where the real writing happens. Every sentence has to be earned twice: once to be written and once to survive the trip to the keyboard. About a third do not make it, and I never miss them.
Three rules I keep
Write the first draft somewhere you cannot publish from.
Type it up the next day, never the same day.
If a sentence does not survive being read aloud, it does not survive.
None of this is efficient. It is not meant to be. The point of a letter like this one is that somebody took their time, and the only way I know to show that is to actually take it.
